description: Original floyd_warshall implementation with explicit domain and deterministic output.
state: finite directed adjacency lists with usize endpoints and nonnegative u64 weights on <=64-bit usize targets
forward: Validate all endpoints in adjacency order before matrix construction. First invalid arc returns InvalidEdge(from,to,V). Otherwise return V-by-V matrix D where D[u,u]=0, D[u,v] is the minimum directed path weight in u128, or None when unreachable. Parallel edges take their minimum; zero-cost cycles do not alter diagonal zero. Checked candidate addition returns DistanceOverflow rather than wrapping.
inverse: In the explicit one-call universe U of finite directed adjacency lists with usize endpoints and nonnegative u64 weights on <=64-bit usize targets crossed with declared returned values, C=U minus R for the forward relation R. C includes incorrect partitions/forests/distances, wrong error details or wrong first-failure precedence. This is the exact specification complement and a partial source-derived approximant of Rust behavior. Allocation failures, panics, timing and traces are outside U.

For each returned y, Pre(y)={x in domain | R(x,y)} retains ALL compatible inputs. For success, preserve every graph satisfying the forward equations and observable canonical ordering; for errors, preserve every graph matching that exact first-failure condition. Parallel alternatives, internal representations and unobserved edge choices are retained whenever compatible. No unique input recovery or executable inverse is claimed.
cost: O(V^3+E) time and O(V^2) auxiliary space including output; cloning one pivot row per stage costs O(V^2) total copying. Allocation failures are outside Result semantics; no flattened V*V index multiplication is used.
checks: four targeted tests twice; strict Clippy; compiled filtered mutation
limitations: Bounded correspondence is not unrestricted proof.
Partial syntax excludes macro expansion and semantic resolution.
